'''Paul Millsap''' (born February 10, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played for 16 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A [[power forward]] from [[Louisiana Tech University]], Millsap was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round (47th pick overall) of the [[2006 NBA draft]] and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]]. He played in Utah until 2013, when he became a member of the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Millsap has also played for the [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He is a four-time [[NBA All-Star]].

==High school career==
Millsap attended [[Grambling High School]], in [[Grambling, Louisiana]], where he played for the Grambling Kittens high school basketball team. The 2003 Louisiana "Mr. Basketball", he was named a fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] and was ranked no. 58 nationally by [[ESPN]].<ref name="Louisiana Tech">{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071213075900/http://www.latechsports.com/player.php?f_name=Paul&l_name=Millsap&sport=MBB&season=05-06|archivedate=December 13, 2007|url=http://www.latechsports.com/player.php?f_name=Paul&l_name=Millsap&sport=MBB&season=05-06|title=Paul Millsap|publisher=Louisiana Tech University|accessdate=March 11, 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== College career ==
In his three-year career at [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]], Millsap averaged 18.6 points, 12.7 rebounds and 2.0 blocks in 92 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/paul-millsap-1.html|title=Paul Millsap|publisher=Sports Reference College Basketball|accessdate=March 11, 2023}}</ref> After becoming the first player to lead NCAA Division I in rebounds in their freshman and sophomore years in 2005, he became the only player in NCAA basketball history with three consecutive seasons leading Division I in rebounding.<ref name="Louisiana Tech"/> As a freshman, Millsap was the [[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] Rookie of the Year and was a second-team all-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] honoree. As a sophomore and junior he was a first-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] honoree. As a junior in 2005–06, Millsap was also a WAC All-Defensive honoree and a finalist for the [[Oscar Robertson Award]].<ref name="Louisiana Tech"/> Following the season, he declared for the [[2006 NBA draft|NBA draft]] on April 4, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060614185413/http://latechsports.com/article.php?article_id=2006_04_04_16:36:51|archivedate=June 14, 2006|title= Junior Forward Paul Millsap Will Forego Senior Season for NBA Draft|url=https://latechsports.com/news/2006/4/4/Junior_Forward_Paul_Millsap_Will_Forego_Senior_Season_for_NBA_Draft.aspx|publisher=Louisiana Tech University|accessdate=March 11, 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Utah Jazz (2006–2013)===
Millsap was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 47th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]], and later signed his rookie scale contract with the Jazz on August 2, 2006. In late 2006, some sports journalists were referring to Millsap as a potential [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] candidate,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://insider.espn.com/nba/insider/columns/story?columnist=hollinger_john&id=2690890 |title=Rookie report: Disappointments and a surprise ROY |date=December 8, 2006 |access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref> an award not traditionally given to players taken so late in the draft. Though the award ultimately went to [[Brandon Roy]], Millsap had a strong first season, leading all rookies with six double-doubles. He finished the 2006–07 season with averages of around 7 [[point (basketball)|points]] per game, 5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, nearly one [[steal (basketball)|steal]] and one [[block (basketball)|block]]; he had season highs of 20 points, 17 rebounds, 4 blocks, 4 steals, 3 assists, and 38 minutes. He played in all 82 of Utah's games. As a solid bench player, the rookie participated in a surprising run to the Conference Finals where his Utah Jazz lost to later NBA champions [[San Antonio Spurs]].

Early in the 2007–08 season, Millsap achieved a new career high of 24 points during a win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He later extended his career high to 28 points against the [[Orlando Magic]] in late December 2007. His next career high came in December 2008 against the [[Boston Celtics]] when he scored 32 points. Millsap had played in 194 straight games since being drafted by the Jazz in 2006; he missed his first game of his professional career on December 26, 2008, against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] due to a sprained posterior cruciate ligament injury in his knee suffered against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] three days prior.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170205181802/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=271221019 Millsap nets career-high 28 as Magic booed in home loss to Jazz]</ref>

During the 2008–09 season, Millsap became the replacement for [[Carlos Boozer]] after the All-Star forward suffered multiple injuries. Millsap's numbers subsequently soared, as he averaged 15.9 points and 10.3 rebounds over 38 starts mid-season.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/millspa01/gamelog/2009/ Paul Millsap 2008–09 Game Log]</ref>

On June 25, 2009, the Jazz tendered a qualifying offer to Millsap, making him a [[restricted free agent]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jazz Makes Qualifying Offer to Millsap |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz_offer_millsap062609.html |date=June 26, 2009 |access-date=July 12, 2009}}</ref> A few weeks later, on July 10, 2009, he signed an offer sheet from the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for $32 million over four years, including $6.2 million in the 2009–10 season, with a $5.6 million signing bonus, with $10.3 million to be paid within seven days of the contract's approval by the NBA.<ref>{{cite web |title=Blazers sign Paul Millsap to offer sheet |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/07/11/millsap.offer.ap/index.html |date=July 12, 2009 |access-date=July 13, 2009}}</ref> The Jazz had the right to match the offer, and did so seven days later, on July 17, 2009.<ref name="siler">{{cite news|url=http://www.sltrib.com/sports/ci_12858425|title=Jazz to match Millsap offer|last=Siler|first=Paul|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=July 17, 2009|access-date=July 17, 2009}}</ref>

Millsap became Utah's permanent starting power forward in 2010–11 after Boozer joined the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Millsap started alongside newly acquired center [[Al Jefferson]]. On November 9, 2010, Millsap scored a career-high 46 points in a 116–114 overtime win over the [[Miami Heat]] outscoring the entire Heat newly formed Big 3. Millsap scored 11 points in 28 seconds at the end of regulation, including three three-pointers, one more than he had made in his entire career before then. He also hit a buzzer-beater to force overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010110914|title=Recap: 2010-11-09 Miami Heat |work=Yahoo! Sports }}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2013–2017)===
[[File:Paul Millsap Atlanta Hawks cropped.jpg|thumb|left|Millsap in 2013]]
On July 10, 2013, after spending the first seven years of his career with the Jazz, Millsap signed a two-year deal with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Windhorst|first=Brian|authorlink=Brian Windhorst |date=July 5, 2013 |title=Sources: Paul Millsap, Hawks agree |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9453695 |access-date=April 2, 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-paul-millsap|title=HAWKS SIGN FORWARD PAUL MILLSAP|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=October 15, 2013}}</ref> On January 30, 2014, Millsap was voted by the coaches to be a reserve on the 2014 East All-Star team.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-forward-paul-millsap-selected-nba-eastern-conference-all-star-reserve HAWKS FORWARD PAUL MILLSAP SELECTED AS NBA EASTERN CONFERENCE ALL-STAR RESERVE]</ref> On March 18, 2014, Millsap recorded his first career triple-double with 19 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in a 118–113 overtime win over the Toronto Raptors.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20140318/TORATL/gameinfo.html Notebook: Hawks 118, Raptors 113 (OT)]</ref>

On January 29, 2015, Millsap earned his second consecutive All-Star nod as a reserve for the Eastern Conference in the [[2015 NBA All-Star Game]]. The Hawks sent four players to the All-Star game, all of whom were selected as reserves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/horford-millsap-teague-eastern-conference-all-stars|title=Al Horford, Paul Millsap and Jeff Teague Named Eastern Conference All-Stars|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2015|access-date=January 31, 2015}}</ref> He went on to help the Hawks finish with a 60–22 record in [[2014–15 Atlanta Hawks season|2014–15]], the team's best finish since [[1993–94 Atlanta Hawks season|1993–94]].<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2442609-playoffs-give-atlanta-hawks-ability-to-cement-best-season-in-franchise-history Playoffs Give Atlanta Hawks Ability to Cement Best Season in Franchise History]</ref> They made it through to the Eastern Conference Finals where they were swept 4–0 by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].

On July 9, 2015, Millsap re-signed with the Hawks to a three-year, $59 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/two-time-all-star-paul-millsap-re-signs-hawks|title=Two-Time All-Star Paul Millsap Re-Signs With The Hawks|date=July 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Broussard|first=Chris|authorlink=Chris Broussard|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13184115|title=Sources: Paul Millsap, Hawks agree to 3-year, $59M contract|publisher=ESPN|date=July 1, 2015|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref> On January 16, 2016, he scored 21 points against the Brooklyn Nets to move past 10,000 for his career.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20160116/BKNATL/gameinfo.html Millsap leads Hawks past Nets 114–86 to snap 2-game skid]</ref> On January 28, he earned his third consecutive All-Star nod as a reserve for the Eastern Conference in the [[2016 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/paul-millsap-named-2016-eastern-conference-all-star-team Paul Millsap Named to 2016 Eastern Conference All-Star Team]</ref> On April 9, 2016, he recorded a season-high 31 points and 16 rebounds in a 118–107 win over the Boston Celtics.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20160409/BOSATL/gameinfo.html Millsap, Teague power Hawks past Celtics 118–107]</ref> The Hawks finished the regular season as the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference with a 48–34 record. In the first round of the playoffs, the Hawks faced the fifth-seeded Boston Celtics, and in a Game 4 loss on April 24, Millsap scored 45 points—a career playoff high and one off his all-time best—and added 13 rebounds. The loss tied the series at 2–2.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20160424/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html Celtics beat Hawks 104–95 in OT, series tied 2–2]</ref> The Hawks went on to defeat the Celtics in six games and moved on to the semi-finals, where they were defeated in four games by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].

In the Hawks' season opener on October 27, 2016, Millsap scored a game-high 28 points on 11-of-20 shooting in a 114–99 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899420|title=Howard, Millsap, Hardaway lead Hawks past Wizards 114–99|work=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}}</ref> On December 19, 2016, he scored a season-high 30 points, including the go-ahead 10-footer with 12.7 seconds left, to help the Hawks defeat the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] 110–108.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899857|title=Hawks overcome Westbrook's 46 to beat Thunder 110–108|work=ESPN.com|date=December 19, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2016}}</ref> On January 1, 2017, he set a new season high with 32 points and had 13 rebounds in a 114–112 overtime win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]], helping the Hawks snap a string of 11 straight losses to San Antonio since 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899374|title=Hardaway powers Hawks to long-awaited OT win over Spurs|work=ESPN.com|date=January 1, 2017|access-date=January 2, 2017}}</ref> On January 26, he was named an Eastern Conference All-Star reserve for the [[2017 NBA All-Star Game]], earning his fourth straight All-Star nod.<ref>{{cite web|last=Whitaker|first=Lang|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/01/26/nba-all-star-reserves-2017-revealed|title=Warriors, Cavaliers dominate selections for NBA All-Star 2017 as reserves are revealed|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2017|access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref> Three days later, he had a season-high 37 points, including the go-ahead layup with 27 seconds remaining in the fourth overtime, to lead the Hawks to a 142–139 win over the [[New York Knicks]]. He also had 19 rebounds, setting another season high, and seven assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900132|title=Paul Millsap (37 points) fuels Hawks past Knicks in 4-overtime game|work=ESPN.com|date=January 29, 2017|access-date=January 29, 2017}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2017–2021)===
[[File:Paul Millsap free throw (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Millsap with the Nuggets in 2020]]
On July 13, 2017, Millsap signed a three-year, $90 million contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-paul-millsap|title=Nuggets Sign Free Agent Paul Millsap|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2017|access-date=July 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2017/07/03/paul-millsap-agrees-3-year-90-deal-denver-nuggets/447316001/|title=Paul Millsap agrees to 3-year, $90 million deal with Denver Nuggets|work=usatoday.com|date=July 2, 2017|access-date=July 2, 2017}}</ref> In his debut for the Nuggets in their season opener on October 18, 2017, Millsap scored 19 points in a 106–96 loss to his former team, the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974766|title=Burks takes over in 4th, Jazz beat Nuggets 106–96|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}}</ref> On November 21, 2017, he was ruled out indefinitely after sustaining a left wrist injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/11/21/report-nuggets-paul-millsap-undergo-wrist-surgery#/|title=Report: Denver Nuggets' Paul Millsap to undergo surgery on left wrist|work=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2017|access-date=November 21, 2017}}</ref> Five days later, he underwent successful reconstructive surgery on his left wrist, ruling him out for several months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/story/millsap-update-112617-2|title=Paul Millsap Injury Update|work=NBA.com|date=November 26, 2017|access-date=November 26, 2017}}</ref> He returned to action on February 27, 2018, against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], recording nine points and seven rebounds in 23½ minutes in a 122–120 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975658|title=Williams helps Clippers rally from 19 down to beat Nuggets|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2018|access-date=February 28, 2018}}</ref> On March 30, 2018, he scored a season-high 36 points to help the Nuggets beat the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] 126–125 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975879|title=Millsap scores 36 as Nuggets top Thunder 126–125 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=March 30, 2018|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref>

On December 3, 2018, Millsap was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played from November 26 to December 2. It was his third career Player of the Week award, and he became the 18th Nuggets player in franchise history to win the award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/paul-millsap-player-of-the-week-120318|title=Paul Millsap Named NBA Western Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref> Four days later against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], Millsap suffered a broken toe in his right foot.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/12/07/report-nuggets-fear-paul-millsap-breaks-right-toe|title=Report: Nuggets forward Paul Millsap suffered broken toe|work=NBA.com|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> He subsequently missed eight games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071209|title=Murray scores 46, hits 9 3s as Nuggets hold off Suns 122–118|work=ESPN.com|date=December 29, 2018|access-date=December 30, 2018|quote=F Paul Millsap returned to action after missing the past eight games with a broken right big toe.}}</ref> On February 13, 2019, he matched a season high with 25 points in a 120–118 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071533|title=Jokic tips in winner as Nuggets beat Kings 120–118|work=ESPN.com|date=February 13, 2019|access-date=February 14, 2019}}</ref> On March 14, he set a new season high with 33 points in a 100–99 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071698|title=Jokic hits buzzer-beater to lift Nuggets over Mavs 100–99|work=ESPN.com|date=March 14, 2019|access-date=March 14, 2019}}</ref>
For the 2019–20 season, Millsap continued to retain his spot in the starting five. 

As players were allowed the option to have a meaningful statement of their choice displayed on the backside of their jersey in support of the [[Black Lives Matter]] movement in the isolated [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA Bubble]], Millsap chose to have "Vote" as his statement, which due to his jersey number 4, ironically appeared as "Vote 4 Millsap", a pun that quickly caught viral attention.<ref name="BLM">{{Cite web|last=Bernstein|first=Brittany|date=July 31, 2020|title=NBA Resumes Season with 'Black Lives Matter' Painted on Court|url=https://www.nationalreview.com/news/nba-resumes-season-with-black-lives-matter-painted-on-court/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924154120/https://www.nationalreview.com/news/nba-resumes-season-with-black-lives-matter-painted-on-court/|archive-date=September 24, 2020|access-date=August 1, 2020|website=National Review}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/paul-millsap-on-his-career-highlights-his-nba-future-and-bringing-change/|title=Q&A: Paul Millsap on his career highlights, his NBA future and bringing change|work=andscape.com|date=September 11, 2020|access-date=December 4, 2024}}</ref> Although his production slightly declined during the playoffs, he kept his starting spot in Denver. With the Nuggets, he reached the Conference Finals for the third time in his career, ultimately losing to eventual NBA champions [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

On December 3, 2020, Millsap re-signed with the Nuggets on a reported one-year deal worth $10 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Denver Nuggets re-sign forward Paul Millsap |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/millsap-resigned-202011 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 18, 2021 |date=December 3, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Denver Nuggets re-sign Paul Millsap to one-year deal |url=https://www.foxsports.com/articles/nba/denver-nuggets-resign-paul-millsap-to-oneyear-deal |website=FOX Sports |access-date=February 18, 2021 |date=December 3, 2020}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2021–2022)===
On September 10, 2021, Millsap signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Paul Millsap |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/09/10/brooklyn-nets-sign-paul-millsap |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 10, 2021 |date=September 10, 2021}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2022) ===
On February 10, 2022, Millsap was traded along with [[James Harden]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Ben Simmons]], [[Seth Curry]], [[Andre Drummond]], and two first-round draft selections.<ref>{{cite web|title=76ers Acquire Seven-Time All-NBA Selection James Harden and Four-Time All-Star Paul Millsap in Trade with Brooklyn Nets|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-acquire-james-harden|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 15, 2022}}</ref> 

In the remaining 28 games that the 76ers had in the regular season, Millsap would suit up in 9 of them, averaging 3.7 points and 2.8 rebounds in 11.8 minutes per game. 

Millsap's final NBA game was Game 1 of the [[2022 NBA playoffs|2022 Eastern Conference Semifinals]] on May 2, 2022. In his final game, Millsap played for 5 and half minutes and recorded 1 rebound and 1 assist as the 76ers fell to the [[Miami Heat]] 106–92.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202205020MIA.html | title=2022 NBA Eastern Conference Semifinals Game 1: 76ers vs Heat, May 2, 2022 }}</ref>

=== Retirement ===
Millsap did not play during the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23]] or [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24]] NBA seasons and subsequently announced his retirement from the league on December 3, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=4-time All-Star Millsap retires after 16 seasons|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42758483/four-all-star-paul-millsap-retires-16-nba-seasons|website=ESPN.com|date=December 3, 2024|access-date=December 3, 2024}}</ref> He retired as one of the eight players in NBA history with 500 3-pointers, 1,000 blocks and 1,000 steals.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-03 |title=4x All-Star, Ex-Nuggets Player Announces NBA Retirement |url=https://www.si.com/nba/nuggets/news/4x-all-star-ex-nuggets-player-announces-nba-retirement-01je6yqwcske |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=Denver Nuggets On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Millsap's brother, [[Elijah Millsap|Elijah]], is a professional basketball player who played for the Utah Jazz.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2015/news/01/25/jazz-sign-elijah-millsap-official-release/ Jazz sign Elijah Millsap to multiyear deal]</ref> His eldest brother, John, played for the [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|UTSA Roadrunners]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hamilton |first1=Linda |title=The Brothers Millsap: John joins Paul on Revue roster |url=https://www.deseret.com/2007/7/13/20029587/the-brothers-millsap-john-joins-paul-on-revue-roster/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=October 3, 2024 |date=July 13, 2007}}</ref>
